name: Autosomal Dominant Congenital Benign Spinal Muscular Atrophy
aliases: AD Congenital Benign Spinal Muscular Atrophy
Spinal Muscular Atrophy, Autosomal Dominant, Congenital, Benign

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Electrophysiological Diagnostic Criteria for Autosomal Dominant Congenital Benign Spinal Muscular Atrophy

criteria.description: Congenital or early infancy onset of proximal muscle weakness with predominant lower limb involvement
Electromyography showing chronic denervation and reinnervation consistent with anterior horn cell disease
Autosomal dominant inheritance pattern with affected first-degree relatives
Preserved cognitive function without developmental delay
Lack of respiratory insufficiency or severe bulbar involvement

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of congenital or early infancy onset proximal muscle weakness with supportive electromyography findings and a positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may assist but causative gene mutations are not fully characterized.

imaging: Muscle MRI showing selective muscle atrophy and fatty infiltration
other: Electromyography demonstrating chronic denervation and reinnervation

distinguishingFeatures: Later onset in childhood or adolescence
Presence of widespread fasciculations without significant weakness

redFlags: Bulbar dysfunction with dysphagia or aspiration
references: Orphanet: Autosomal dominant congenital benign spinal muscular atrophy (ORPHA:1216)
Dubowitz V. Muscle Disorders in Childhood. 3rd ed. Saunders; 2007.
